quotes.quote: IL-4 priming increased the number of NF-κB-p65 peaks from 25,428 to 48,507 ( Figure 2A ) and the occupancy of LPS-activated NF-κB-p65 at 26,440 genomic regions ( Figure 2B ; Table S1 ).
The single-ended mRNA sequence reads were analyzed using the nf-core/rnaseq v3.0 pipeline ( Ewels et al., 2020 ).

G1.rationale: The principal result (NF-κB-p65 peak counts) is produced by computational analysis of ChIP-seq data, which a third party can re-run from deposited raw sequencing data.

quotes.quote: IL-4 priming increased the number of NF-κB-p65 peaks from 25,428 to 48,507 ( Figure 2A ) and the occupancy of LPS-activated NF-κB-p65 at 26,440 genomic regions ( Figure 2B ; Table S1 ).

G2.rationale: A primary numerical endpoint is explicitly stated: the number of NF-κB-p65 peaks in IL-4-primed vs non-polarized LPS-activated BMDMs.

quotes.quote: Sequencing data sets performed in this study are available at the NCBI GEO under accession numbers: GSE181223 . Publicly available, published ChIP-seq data sets can be accessed on the following GEO accession numbers: GSE159630 and GSE151015 .

G3.rationale: The deposit listing shows only GSE159630 (a public dataset from Hoeksema et al., 2021), which is not the raw input for the target; the paper's own data are in GSE181223, which is not in the listing. Thus the listed files are not the analysis inputs for the target.

quotes.quote: ChIP-seq read alignment and filtering were carried out using our ChIP-seq command line pipeline ( Barta, 2011 ). Reads were mapped to the mouse reference genome ( mm10 ) using the default parameters of BWA MEM aligner ( Li and Durbin, 2009 ).
MACS2 ( Zhang et al., 2008 ) was used to call peaks at 5% false discovery rate (FDR).
To determine differentially bound NFκB-p65 genomic regions, we first used DiffBind ( Ross-Innes et al., 2012 ) to generate a consensus peak set with minOverlap=2 for all samples.

G4.rationale: The ChIP-seq analysis method (alignment, peak calling, differential binding) is described with sufficient detail and references to implement without original code.

specification.exact_target: Number of NF-κB-p65 peaks in LPS-activated non-polarized vs IL-4-primed WT BMDMs: 25,428 vs 48,507.
specification.blind_target: The number of NF-κB-p65 binding sites (peaks) detected by ChIP-seq in LPS-activated wild-type bone marrow-derived macrophages, comparing cells that were non-polarized versus cells that were primed with IL-4.
specification.target_location: Figure 2A and Results section 'Prior IL-4 exposure approximately doubles the LPS-activated NF-κB-p65 cistrome, resulting in an altered enhancer landscape'

location_quotes.quote: IL-4 priming increased the number of NF-κB-p65 peaks from 25,428 to 48,507 ( Figure 2A ) and the occupancy of LPS-activated NF-κB-p65 at 26,440 genomic regions ( Figure 2B ; Table S1 ).
(A) Bar plot visualization of the overall number of binding sites for NF-κB-p65 from ChIP-seq experiments in IL-4-primed and non-polarized WT and Stat6 −/− BMDMs following LPS activation.

method_quotes.quote: ChIP-seq read alignment and filtering were carried out using our ChIP-seq command line pipeline ( Barta, 2011 ). Reads were mapped to the mouse reference genome ( mm10 ) using the default parameters of BWA MEM aligner ( Li and Durbin, 2009 ).
MACS2 ( Zhang et al., 2008 ) was used to call peaks at 5% false discovery rate (FDR).
To determine differentially bound NFκB-p65 genomic regions, we first used DiffBind ( Ross-Innes et al., 2012 ) to generate a consensus peak set with minOverlap=2 for all samples.

specification.input_notes: The paper's own sequencing data are deposited under GEO accession GSE181223 (S0137), but this accession is not present in the provided deposit listing. The listing contains only GSE159630, which is a public dataset from Hoeksema et al., 2021 (S0137, S0291, S0292) and is not the raw input for the target NF-κB-p65 peak counts. Therefore, the required input files are not among the listed files.
